claims.text: Pods are ephemeral; a replacement Pod is a new Pod with its own IP address, so the set of Pod IPs behind an app changes over time and a stored Pod IP can stop pointing at the app.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Services (Motivation: Pods are ephemeral, IP addresses change); outputs/stage-2/scripts/k8s/service.txt

claims.text: A Service selects Pods with a label selector and creates no Pods itself; it gets a virtual IP address (cluster IP) that no Pod owns.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Services (Defining a Service; Virtual IPs and Service Proxies)

claims.text: A Service's cluster IP is allocated when the Service is created and stays the same for the Service's lifetime, even when its Pods are replaced.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Services (ClusterIP; spec.clusterIP immutable); outputs service.txt ('same as before: yes')

claims.text: A connection to the Service's cluster IP and port is forwarded to targetPort on one of the Pods matched by the selector; connections are spread across those Pods.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Services (Defining a Service: port/targetPort; traffic distributed across endpoints)

claims.text: Kubernetes keeps the addresses of the Pods matching a Service's selector (EndpointSlices) up to date as Pods are replaced or scaled; kubectl describe service shows them in the Endpoints line as IP:targetPort.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Services (EndpointSlices); executed kubectl describe service api -n donhang

claims.text: If a Service manifest omits spec.type, the type is ClusterIP, which makes the Service reachable only from within the cluster.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Services (Service type ClusterIP: default; reachable only from within the cluster)

claims.text: deploy/k8s/lessons/web-service.yaml@stage-2: Service web in donhang, selector app: web, port 80, targetPort 80, no type.

scripts/k8s/service.sh@stage-2 applies web-deployment.yaml then the Service; helpers cluster_ip, web_pod_ips, fetch_title (kubectl run caddy:2.10.0 Pod, wget, prints <title>); deletes all app=web Pods; output service.txt.
The default page served by the caddy:2.10.0 image has the title 'Caddy works!'; Caddy listens on port 80 in the container with the image's default Caddyfile.
claims.source_hint: outputs/stage-2/scripts/k8s/service.txt; caddy image default Caddyfile (:80, file_server)

claims.text: service.sh leaves the Deployment web and the Service web running (no cleanup at the end).
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2 scripts/k8s/service.sh (ends after second fetch_title)
